site.name: Qararit
site.title: We Have Let So Many Qirats Slip Away
site.tagline: Great rewards the Prophet ﷺ told us about. Let us seize them.
site.pilot_notice: Pilot version: translations are drafts awaiting scholarly and linguistic review.

origin.text: “We have let so many qirats slip away.”
origin.speaker: 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both)
origin.context: Ibn 'Umar was told that Abu Hurayrah was saying: “Whoever follows a funeral will have one qirat.” He said: “Abu Hurayrah narrates too much to us.” So he sent someone to 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her), and she confirmed what Abu Hurayrah said. Then Ibn 'Umar said: “We have let so many qirats slip away.” Before that, he used to pray over the deceased and then leave.
origin.note: In a narration of Muslim (945) through Salim: “We have wasted so many qirats.”

janaza.title: The Virtue of Attending a Funeral
janaza.lead: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
janaza.text: “Whoever attends the funeral until he prays over it will have one qirat, and whoever attends until it is buried will have two qirats.” It was asked, “And what are the two qirats?” He said, “Like two huge mountains.”
reward: will have one qirat
will have two qirats
Like two huge mountains
janaza.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
janaza.meaning: Whoever attends the funeral prayer of a Muslim receives one qirat of reward, and if he stays with the funeral until the burial is complete, he receives two. A qirat here is an immense measure of reward: the Prophet ﷺ described it as being like a huge mountain, and in a narration of Muslim: “The smaller of the two is like Uhud.”
janaza.imani: Two huge mountains of reward, for an hour spent with your brother at the end of his road. On that day nothing benefits the deceased like the prayers and supplications of his brothers, and so, out of His generosity, Allah rewards the one who shows up with more than he could ever imagine.
janaza.tarbawi: When a funeral is announced at a nearby mosque, don't ask whether you knew the deceased; the reward is not limited to people you know. Take your child who is old enough with you once, so they learn that accompanying a Muslim's funeral is his right, not a social courtesy.
janaza.action: When you hear of a Muslim's funeral at a nearby mosque, attend the prayer over him; and if you can, walk with the procession to the cemetery and stay until the burial is complete.
janaza.caveat: In a narration of al-Bukhari (47), the Prophet ﷺ made it conditional on being done “out of faith and seeking reward”, that is, hoping for Allah's reward. The second qirat is for the one who stays until the burial.
commentary: Fath al-Bari by Ibn Hajar: Book of Funerals, chapter on the virtue of following funerals
Sharh an-Nawawi on Sahih Muslim: Book of Funerals

story.text: Ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) was told of Abu Hurayrah's hadith about the qirat, so he sent someone to ask 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her), and she confirmed what Abu Hurayrah had said. Ibn 'Umar struck the ground with the pebbles he had in his hand and said: “We have let so many qirats slip away.”

tahlil-100.title: Saying the Tahlil 100 Times a Day
tahlil-100.lead: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
tahlil-100.text: “Whoever says, ‘There is no god but Allah, alone, without partner; His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things,’ 100 times in a day, it will equal for him the freeing of 10 slaves, 100 good deeds will be recorded for him, 100 bad deeds will be erased from him, and it will be a protection for him from Satan on that day until evening. And no one will bring anything better than what he brought, except someone who did more than that.”
reward: it will equal for him the freeing of 10 slaves
100 good deeds will be recorded for him
100 bad deeds will be erased from him
it will be a protection for him from Satan on that day until evening
tahlil-100.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
tahlil-100.meaning: “It will equal the freeing of 10 slaves” means its reward equals the reward of freeing ten slaves. On top of that, one hundred good deeds are recorded for the one who says it, one hundred bad deeds are erased, and he is guarded from Satan for the rest of his day until evening. No one surpasses him except someone who says it more than he did.
tahlil-100.imani: A hundred good deeds written, a hundred bad deeds erased, and a fortress against Satan for your whole day, through words you can say in a few minutes. This is how the Most Generous gives: a small deed, and a reward out of all proportion to the effort. Only the heedless miss it.
tahlil-100.tarbawi: Tie this remembrance to a fixed part of your morning, like sitting after the Fajr prayer or your commute to work. A habit anchored to a set time and place takes root faster than one that waits for free time.
tahlil-100.action: Say it early in your day: the protection from Satan in the hadith lasts “on that day until evening”, so the earlier you say it, the longer you benefit.
commentary: Sharh an-Nawawi on Sahih Muslim: Book of Remembrance and Supplication, chapter on the virtue of tahlil and tasbih
Fath al-Bari by Ibn Hajar: Book of Supplications, chapter on the virtue of tahlil

poem.meaning: Indeed, everything other than Allah is vain and fleeting.
poem.poet: Labid ibn Rabi'ah (may Allah be pleased with him)
poem.note: The Prophet ﷺ said about it: “The truest word spoken by a poet is the word of Labid.”

subhan-100.title: Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi, 100 Times
subhan-100.lead: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
subhan-100.text: “Whoever says, ‘Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi (Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Him),’ 100 times in a day, his sins will be wiped away, even if they are like the foam of the sea.”
reward: his sins will be wiped away, even if they are like the foam of the sea
subhan-100.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
subhan-100.meaning: “Subhan Allah” declares Allah free of every imperfection, and “wa bihamdihi” praises Him for His perfection. Whoever says it one hundred times in his day has his sins taken off him, even if they are as many as the foam that rises on the waves of the sea.
subhan-100.imani: The foam of the sea cannot be counted, and yet light words, said sincerely, wipe it away. This does not make light of sin; it shows how vast Allah's mercy is, and calls on every servant never to despair, however many his mistakes.
subhan-100.tarbawi: One hundred takes only a few minutes. Make it the companion of a trip you take every day, such as the walk to the mosque or waiting for an appointment, until it becomes a habit that needs no reminder.
subhan-100.action: Say it one hundred times in your day, all at once or spread out; it only takes a few minutes.
subhan-100.caveat: Most scholars say the sins meant here are the minor ones; major sins require repentance.
commentary: Sharh an-Nawawi on Sahih Muslim: Book of Remembrance and Supplication, chapter on the virtue of tahlil and tasbih
Fath al-Bari by Ibn Hajar: Book of Supplications, chapter on the virtue of tasbih

kalimatan.title: Two Phrases Light on the Tongue
kalimatan.text: “Two phrases are light on the tongue, heavy on the Scale, and beloved to the Most Merciful: ‘Subhan Allahi l-'Azim (Glory be to Allah, the Magnificent)’ and ‘Subhan Allahi wa bihamdihi (Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Him).’”
reward: heavy on the Scale
beloved to the Most Merciful
kalimatan.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
kalimatan.meaning: Two easy phrases that cost no effort, yet their reward is so great that they weigh heavily in a servant's Scale on the Day of Judgement, and Allah loves them, because they declare Him free of imperfection, magnify Him and praise Him.
kalimatan.imani: Light on the tongue, so no one has an excuse to leave them. Heavy on the Scale, so no sensible person takes them lightly. Beloved to the Most Merciful, and for one who loves Him, that alone is enough. Al-Bukhari chose this hadith to close his Sahih.
kalimatan.tarbawi: Teach them to your child at bedtime with a simple meaning: “Subhan Allah” means Allah is free of every flaw, and “wa bihamdihi” means we thank and praise Him. Then make them the family's remembrance in the car, instead of silence or idle talk.
kalimatan.action: Repeat them while waiting, on the road and while working; they need no special time.
commentary: Fath al-Bari by Ibn Hajar: Book of Tawhid, the last hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari (7563)
Sharh an-Nawawi on Sahih Muslim: Book of Remembrance and Supplication

sayyid-istighfar.title: The Master of Seeking Forgiveness
sayyid-istighfar.text: “The master of all ways of seeking forgiveness is that you say: ‘O Allah, You are my Lord; there is no god but You. You created me and I am Your servant, and I hold to Your covenant and Your promise as far as I am able. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge before You Your favour upon me, and I acknowledge before You my sin, so forgive me, for none forgives sins but You.’ He said: Whoever says it during the day with firm faith in it and dies on that day before evening, he is among the people of Paradise; and whoever says it at night with firm faith in it and dies before morning, he is among the people of Paradise.”
reward: he is among the people of Paradise
sayyid-istighfar.narrator: Shaddad ibn Aws (may Allah be pleased with him)
sayyid-istighfar.meaning: This is the most comprehensive way of asking forgiveness: it affirms that Allah is the Lord and you are His servant, acknowledges His blessings and your shortcomings, and then asks for forgiveness. “I acknowledge” renders the Arabic “abu'u”: I admit and confess. Whoever says it with firm conviction in its meaning and dies before evening, or before morning, is among the people of Paradise.
sayyid-istighfar.imani: In this supplication the servant stands between two things: Allah's blessing, which he acknowledges, and his own sin, which he admits. Whoever combines recognising Allah's favour with recognising his own failings has come to know his Lord and himself, and that is the door to forgiveness.
sayyid-istighfar.tarbawi: Memorise it this week, one sentence at a time, and keep it written on a card by your bed. And don't rush through it: the reward is tied to saying it “with firm faith in it”, believing its meanings with a present heart.
sayyid-istighfar.action: Memorise it, and say it once in your morning remembrance and once in your evening remembrance.
sayyid-istighfar.caveat: The reward is conditional on saying it “with firm faith in it”, meaning believing its meaning in your heart, not merely repeating it with the tongue.
commentary: Fath al-Bari by Ibn Hajar: Book of Supplications, chapter on the best way of seeking forgiveness

wudu-shahada.title: The Two Testimonies after Wudu'
wudu-shahada.lead: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
wudu-shahada.text: “There is none among you who performs wudu' and does it thoroughly (or: completes it fully), then says, ‘I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the servant of Allah and His Messenger,’ except that the 8 gates of Paradise are opened for him, and he may enter through whichever of them he wishes.”
reward: the 8 gates of Paradise are opened for him, and he may enter through whichever of them he wishes
wudu-shahada.narrator: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), as narrated by 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir
wudu-shahada.meaning: Whoever completes his wudu' and does it well, then pronounces the two testimonies of faith, has all eight gates of Paradise opened for him as an honour, and may enter through whichever he wishes. “Thoroughly (or: fully)” reflects a narrator's uncertainty between two Arabic words; both mean the same thing: completing the wudu' properly.
wudu-shahada.imani: Eight gates are opened for you, all of them, and then the choice is left to you. An honour worthy of a generous King, given for a wudu' you make several times a day and a testimony you have known by heart since childhood.
wudu-shahada.tarbawi: Give your wudu' a fixed ending: don't leave the spot until you have said the two testimonies. If there are children at home, say it aloud, and they will learn it from you without a lesson.
wudu-shahada.action: After every wudu', say the two testimonies of faith before you walk away.
wudu-shahada.caveat: The condition is to perform wudu' thoroughly, that is, to complete it properly.
commentary: Sharh an-Nawawi on Sahih Muslim: Book of Purification, chapter on the recommended remembrance after wudu'

story.text: It was 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir's (may Allah be pleased with him) turn to tend the camels. When he came back, he found the Prophet ﷺ speaking to the people and heard him mention the virtue of one who performs wudu' and then prays two rak'ahs, turning to them with his heart. He said, “How excellent this is!” Then he found 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) in front of him, saying, “What he said before this was even better,” and 'Umar told him the hadith of the two testimonies after wudu'.

adhan-dua.title: The Supplication after the Call to Prayer
adhan-dua.lead: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
adhan-dua.text: “Whoever says, when he hears the call to prayer, ‘O Allah, Lord of this perfect call and of the prayer about to be established, grant Muhammad al-Wasilah and al-Fadilah, and raise him to the praised station that You have promised him,’ my intercession will be due to him on the Day of Resurrection.”
reward: my intercession will be due to him on the Day of Resurrection
adhan-dua.narrator: Jabir ibn 'Abdillah (may Allah be pleased with them both)
adhan-dua.meaning: “The perfect call” is the adhan. “Al-Wasilah” is a rank in Paradise, as stated in Sahih Muslim (384), and “the praised station” is the station of intercession. Whoever makes this supplication on hearing the adhan becomes deserving of the Prophet's ﷺ intercession on the Day of Resurrection.
adhan-dua.imani: The adhan comes five times every day, and each time a door opens to the Prophet's ﷺ intercession on the day of greatest distress. How many calls to prayer have passed us by while we were busy! The next chance is only a few hours away.
adhan-dua.tarbawi: Make the adhan a signal to pause: lower whatever you are listening to, repeat after the muezzin, then say this supplication. You could also hang it, written out, near the front door so the little ones memorise it over time.
adhan-dua.action: When the adhan ends, say this supplication. You have five chances every day.
commentary: Fath al-Bari by Ibn Hajar: Book of the Adhan, chapter on supplication at the call to prayer

jamaah-27.title: The Virtue of Praying in Congregation
jamaah-27.lead: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
jamaah-27.text: “Prayer in congregation surpasses the prayer of one praying alone by 27 degrees.”
reward: by 27 degrees
jamaah-27.narrator: 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both)
jamaah-27.meaning: “One praying alone” renders the Arabic “al-fadhdh”, the person who prays by himself. A person's prayer with the congregation exceeds his prayer alone in reward by twenty-seven degrees.
jamaah-27.imani: Twenty-seven degrees in every prayer, five times a day. If these were profits you could see, no one would give them up; they are left only because they are hidden from the eye. The believer sees with his heart what Allah has promised, as though it were before him.
jamaah-27.tarbawi: Pick one prayer whose congregation you usually miss and make it your goal this week. Set an alarm ten minutes before the iqamah, and take your son along; habits built in childhood last.
jamaah-27.action: Make a point of praying the obligatory prayers in congregation at the mosque, and if you usually miss them, start by adding one prayer a day.
jamaah-27.caveat: The hadith of Abu Hurayrah says “twenty-five times” (al-Bukhari 647). Scholars reconciled the two narrations in several ways, which Ibn Hajar mentions in Fath al-Bari.
commentary: Fath al-Bari by Ibn Hajar: Book of the Adhan, chapter on the virtue of praying in congregation

isha-fajr.title: 'Isha' and Fajr in Congregation
isha-fajr.lead: 'Uthman ibn 'Affan (may Allah be pleased with him) said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
isha-fajr.text: “Whoever prays 'Isha' in congregation, it is as if he stood half the night in prayer; and whoever prays the dawn prayer in congregation, it is as if he prayed the whole night.”
reward: it is as if he stood half the night in prayer
it is as if he prayed the whole night
isha-fajr.narrator: 'Uthman ibn 'Affan (may Allah be pleased with him)
isha-fajr.meaning: Whoever prays 'Isha' with the congregation has the reward of one who stood half the night in prayer, and whoever prays the dawn prayer with the congregation has the reward of one who stood the whole night.
isha-fajr.imani: Allah records a whole night of prayer for the one who prays two prayers with the congregation. They are among the heaviest prayers on the soul, which is why their reward is so great; whoever bears their weight patiently will taste the sweetness of the promise.
isha-fajr.tarbawi: The secret of Fajr lies in the evening: whoever sleeps early after 'Isha' wakes for Fajr. Keep your phone away from your bed, and agree with a friend or neighbour that whoever wakes first will wake the other.
isha-fajr.action: Make praying 'Isha' and Fajr at the mosque your daily priority, and sleep early to help yourself wake for Fajr.
isha-fajr.caveat: In the narration of Abu Dawud (555): “Whoever prays 'Isha' and Fajr in congregation, it is like standing a whole night in prayer.” So some scholars understood that the reward of the whole night is for the one who prays both.
commentary: Sharh an-Nawawi on Sahih Muslim: Book of Mosques and Places of Prayer, chapter on the virtue of praying 'Isha' and the dawn prayer in congregation

rawatib-12.title: Twelve Rak'ahs Every Day
rawatib-12.lead: Umm Habibah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
rawatib-12.text: “Whoever prays 12 rak'ahs in a day and night, a house will be built for him in Paradise because of them.”
reward: a house will be built for him in Paradise because of them
rawatib-12.narrator: Umm Habibah (may Allah be pleased with her)
rawatib-12.wording: The wording is Muslim's; the details are in at-Tirmidhi.
rawatib-12.meaning: These are the regular sunnah prayers that accompany the obligatory prayers; a narration of Muslim says: “voluntary, besides the obligatory.” Whoever keeps them up every day has a house built for him in Paradise. Umm Habibah said: “I have not left them since I heard them.”
rawatib-12.imani: A house in Paradise, built for you rak'ah by rak'ah as you go about your daily prayers. The Companions did not hear such things and move on; for them, hearing was the start of a deed that never stopped.
rawatib-12.tarbawi: Start with the easiest: the two rak'ahs of Fajr and the two of Maghrib. Once they are steady for two weeks, add the two after 'Isha', then the sunnah of Zuhr. Gradual building lasts longer than one day's enthusiasm.
rawatib-12.action: At-Tirmidhi (415) gives the details, and al-Albani graded it authentic: four before Zuhr and two after it, two after Maghrib, two after 'Isha', and two before Fajr.
commentary: Sharh an-Nawawi on Sahih Muslim: Book of the Prayer of Travellers, chapter on the virtue of the regular sunnah prayers

story.text: When Umm Habibah (may Allah be pleased with her) narrated this hadith, she said: “I have not left them since I heard them from the Messenger of Allah.” Then 'Anbasah, who heard it from her, said: “I have not left them since I heard them from Umm Habibah,” and after him 'Amr ibn Aws said the same, and then an-Nu'man ibn Salim: one generation passing on to the next a deed that is never abandoned.

visit-sick.title: The Virtue of Visiting the Sick
visit-sick.lead: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
visit-sick.text: “Whoever visits a sick person remains in the khurfah of Paradise.” It was asked, “O Messenger of Allah, what is the khurfah of Paradise?” He said, “Its harvest of fruit.”
reward: remains in the khurfah of Paradise
visit-sick.narrator: Thawban, the freed servant of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ
visit-sick.meaning: “The khurfah of Paradise” is its fruit that is picked, as the Prophet ﷺ explained. Whoever visits a sick person is, throughout his visit, as if he were in the gardens of Paradise gathering its fruit; and one narration adds: “until he returns.”
visit-sick.imani: As long as you are with the sick person, you are gathering the fruits of Paradise. The visit you think of as a social duty is, in reality, a walk through a garden of the Hereafter, and the patient you comfort is opening a door of grace for you.
visit-sick.tarbawi: Set yourself one visit to a sick person every week, whether a relative, a neighbour or a colleague. Keep the visit short, pray for him, and don't burden him with questions about the details of his illness.
visit-sick.action: Visit a sick person you know, a relative, neighbour or colleague, even briefly, and pray for his recovery.
commentary: Sharh an-Nawawi on Sahih Muslim: Book of Righteousness, Keeping Ties and Manners, chapter on the virtue of visiting the sick

story.text: One day the Prophet ﷺ asked his Companions: “Who among you is fasting today?” Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said, “I am.” Then he asked who had followed a funeral, who had fed a poor person, and who had visited a sick person, and each time Abu Bakr said, “I have.” The Prophet ﷺ said: “These never come together in a person except that he enters Paradise.”

silat-rahim.title: Keeping the Ties of Kinship
silat-rahim.lead: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
silat-rahim.text: “Whoever would love for his provision to be expanded and his lifespan to be lengthened, let him keep the ties of kinship.”
reward: his provision to be expanded
his lifespan to be lengthened
silat-rahim.narrator: Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him)
silat-rahim.meaning: Whoever keeps up ties with his relatives through visits, checking on them and kindness, Allah expands his provision. “His lifespan to be lengthened” (literally, “his trace to be delayed”) means that his appointed term is postponed and his life is blessed.
silat-rahim.imani: Provision that grows, and a trace that lives on after you are gone. Allah promised the one who keeps family ties what all people strive for, but by a road many neglect: checking on a relative you had forgotten, and reconnecting a tie that was broken.
silat-rahim.tarbawi: Write down the names of five relatives you haven't contacted in a while, and reach out to one each week. If there is coldness between you, begin with a short message of salam and a prayer for them.
silat-rahim.action: Call a relative today whom you haven't been in touch with for a while, visit them, or help them however you can.
silat-rahim.caveat: Scholars hold two views on the meaning of a longer life: blessing in it and being guided to good deeds, or a real increase relative to what is in the knowledge of the angels.
commentary: Sharh an-Nawawi on Sahih Muslim: Book of Righteousness and Keeping Ties, chapter on keeping ties of kinship
Fath al-Bari by Ibn Hajar: Book of Manners, chapter on whoever has his provision expanded through keeping ties of kinship

dalla-khayr.title: Guiding Others to Good
dalla-khayr.lead: A man came asking for someone to give him a mount, and another man said, “I will direct him to someone who can give him a mount.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
dalla-khayr.text: “Whoever guides to good will have the like of the reward of the one who does it.”
reward: will have the like of the reward of the one who does it
dalla-khayr.narrator: Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari (may Allah be pleased with him)
dalla-khayr.meaning: Whoever guides someone else to a good deed, or directs him to someone who can help him do it, Allah records for him the same reward as the one who does it. The Prophet ﷺ said this about a man who directed a person in need to someone who could help him.
dalla-khayr.imani: A word from you may lead to a deed repeated for years, its reward flowing to you without your knowing. This is the vastness of Allah's grace: He gives the one who points to good the like of the doer's reward, and the doer loses nothing of his own.
dalla-khayr.tarbawi: When you share a hadith, choose someone you know needs it and send it to them personally, with a word of your own. A message addressed to a particular person has more effect than a general post no one stops to read.
dalla-khayr.action: Share one of these hadiths with someone you love; if they act on it, you will have the like of their reward.
commentary: Sharh an-Nawawi on Sahih Muslim: Book of Leadership, chapter on the virtue of helping one who sets out in Allah's cause

ramadan-qadr.title: Fasting Ramadan and Praying on Laylat al-Qadr
ramadan-qadr.lead: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
ramadan-qadr.text: “Whoever stands in prayer on Laylat al-Qadr out of faith and seeking reward will have his past sins forgiven; and whoever fasts Ramadan out of faith and seeking reward will have his past sins forgiven.”
reward: will have his past sins forgiven
ramadan-qadr.narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
ramadan-qadr.meaning: “Out of faith” means believing in its obligation and in Allah's promise, and “seeking reward” means hoping for reward from Allah, not to show off and not out of habit. Whoever fasts Ramadan in this way, or stands in prayer on Laylat al-Qadr in this way, has his past sins forgiven.
ramadan-qadr.imani: One night, if its prayer is accepted, wipes away the sins of all that has passed. Whoever knows its worth will not think ten nights too much to seek it in. What is the fatigue of ten nights next to the forgiveness of all one's past sins?
ramadan-qadr.tarbawi: Plan the last ten nights before they arrive: lighten your commitments, arrange your sleep, and set a portion of worship for each night. And involve your family: when the last ten began, the Prophet ﷺ would stay up at night and wake his family (al-Bukhari 2024).
ramadan-qadr.action: Renew your intention before Ramadan, and make a point of praying on all of the last ten nights so that you catch Laylat al-Qadr.
ramadan-qadr.caveat: The forgiveness is conditional on faith and seeking reward, and most scholars hold that minor sins are meant.
commentary: Fath al-Bari by Ibn Hajar: Book of Fasting, chapter on whoever fasts Ramadan out of faith, seeking reward, with intention
Sharh an-Nawawi on Sahih Muslim: Book of the Prayer of Travellers, chapter on encouragement to pray at night in Ramadan

arafah-ashura.title: Fasting the Days of 'Arafah and 'Ashura'
arafah-ashura.lead: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
arafah-ashura.text: “Fasting the day of 'Arafah: I hope from Allah that it will expiate the year before it and the year after it. And fasting the day of 'Ashura': I hope from Allah that it will expiate the year before it.”
reward: that it will expiate the year before it and the year after it
that it will expiate the year before it
arafah-ashura.narrator: Abu Qatadah al-Ansari (may Allah be pleased with him)
arafah-ashura.wording: An excerpt from a longer hadith.
arafah-ashura.meaning: Fasting the day of 'Arafah, the 9th of Dhul-Hijjah, expiates the sins of two years: the past one and the coming one. Fasting the day of 'Ashura', the 10th of Muharram, expiates the sins of the past year.
arafah-ashura.imani: Fasting a single day expiates two years. The virtuous days are seasonal gifts that pass quickly and return only a year later, and we may not live to see them again; so let us welcome them like someone who fears they won't come back.
arafah-ashura.tarbawi: Add the day of 'Arafah and the 9th and 10th of Muharram to your phone calendar with a reminder two days before. Fast with your family and break the fast together, so your children learn that these days have a special place.
arafah-ashura.action: Put a reminder in your calendar for these two days. It is recommended to fast the 9th along with 'Ashura', because the Prophet ﷺ said: “If I live until next year, I will fast the ninth” (Muslim 1134).
arafah-ashura.caveat: Fasting on 'Arafah is recommended for those not performing Hajj; the Prophet ﷺ did not fast on the day of 'Arafah while he was standing there (al-Bukhari 1988). Most scholars hold that the expiation is for minor sins.
commentary: Sharh an-Nawawi on Sahih Muslim: Book of Fasting, chapter on the recommendation to fast three days of every month and the days of 'Arafah and 'Ashura'
